name: Product design debate
description: PM, Engineer and Architect cross-examine a feature over the bus (specialists join when the brief needs them) and design it top-down: the high-level decisions, then the components that realise them, then the testable requirements, each level tracing to the one above; only blocking business questions reach the user.
whenToUse: A new feature or product change needs a spec: scope, requirements, design and decisions.

texts.definition-of-done: The spec is done when: the user problem and success criteria are explicit; goals and non-goals are listed; every requirement is testable; each key decision has its rationale and the rejected alternative; risks have mitigations; open questions have an owner. Number every requirement R1, R2, …; each traces to the H and C points it details, and every C point is detailed by a requirement or deferred.
texts.design-guide: The high-level design makes the decisions that shape the solution: scope, boundaries, data and control flow, the approach with the alternatives rejected, the main risks. Number each decision H1, H2, … and leave component and requirement detail to the next levels.
texts.components-guide: The component design realises the high-level decisions: each component or interface C1, C2, … with its responsibility, its interfaces and data, and the H decisions it realises (tracesTo). Every H decision is realised by a component or deferred with its reason.

phases.title: Explore
phases.goal: Each role analyses the brief from its perspective and states a position: proposals, concerns and questions.
instructions: Read the codebase areas the brief touches before forming your position.

phases.title: Debate
phases.goal: Challenge and refine the positions until the team agrees on scope, approach and architecture.

phases.title: Decide
phases.goal: Ask the user only the questions that block the team and that only the user can answer.

phases.title: High-level design
phases.goal: Write the high-level decisions the team agreed on and get them approved by the PM and the Engineer.

phases.title: Component design
phases.goal: Design the components and interfaces that realise the high-level decisions, and get the Architect to approve them.

phases.title: Spec
phases.goal: Write the testable requirements that detail the design and get them approved by the Architect and the Engineer.

triggers: A scope or priority trade-off that changes what users get
A cost, licensing or infrastructure commitment
Business context the team cannot see
